Home guide

From muddy yard to finished driveway

Drag the line to see the change. A paved driveway stays clean in the monsoon, drains through its joints and can be lifted and re-laid if a pipe ever needs work.

BeforeAfter
How your driveway gets laid
  1. Dig and level

    Soft soil comes out and the ground is shaped to slope gently away from the house.

  2. Build the base

    Crushed stone is spread and compacted in layers. This is what carries the weight.

  3. Spread the sand bed

    About 30 mm of sharp sand, screeded flat, gives every block an even seat.

  4. Lay and cut

    Blocks go down in your pattern, with the border laid first and cut pieces at the edges.

  5. Vibrate and fill joints

    A plate compactor beds the blocks and fine sand is brushed into every joint to lock them.

Most home driveways take two to four days to lay, depending on size and weather.

How it's made

From mix to your site

01

Batch

Cement, stone dust, grit and pigment are weighed for every batch.

02

Press

Vibration and pressure pack the mix tight into steel moulds.

03

Cure

Blocks are kept moist while they cure, so they reach full strength.

04

Check

Sample blocks are checked for size, strength and water absorption.

05

Dispatch

Counted, stacked and loaded for your site from Mandideep.
